chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the husband and wife who both die, so the inheritors of the woman come and claim the dower upon the inheritors of the man. He said: 'And they had both died and the inheritance was distributed?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.'

I said: 'And if the woman was alive, and she came after the death of her husband to claim her dower?' He said: 'There is nothing for her, and she had stayed with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband died.'

I said: 'And if she died while he was alive, so her inheritors came seeking her dower from him?' He said: 'And she had stayed with him until she died not seeking it?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.'
I said: 'And if he divorced her, so she came seeking her dower?' He said: 'And she had stayed not seeking it until he divorced her, there is nothing for her.'

I said: 'So when is the limit of that which, if she were to seek it, it would be for her?' He said: 'If it was gifted to her and she entered his house, then she seeks it after that, so there is nothing for her.'
It is sufficient for her if she makes him swear an oath by Allah that there is no dower for her with him, neither little nor much.

key_terms.تَسْتَحْلِفَ: To make him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: When do the heirs of a wife lose the right to claim her dower after her husband's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'sukut' (silence) as a form of implied acceptance of debt, establishing that a wife's failure to claim her dower (mahr) during the marriage constitutes a waiver of the right to sue for it after his death or divorce. It distinguishes between the full claimable amount and the residual right to exact an oath of non-payment once the marital bond is dissolved, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on preventing perpetual financial liability for the husband. This ruling underscores the Shia view that dower is a right of the wife that can be extinguished by her inaction, contrasting with some Sunni schools that view it as a fixed debt.
